2021_21_2_a_troy_school_district_0621_si.paragraph: Draft federal awards supplemental information for Troy School District for the year ended June 30, 2021, delivered to the Board of Education with independent auditor's reports dated October 5, 2021. The package holds the Schedule of Expenditures of Federal Awards, a reconciliation of financial-statement federal revenue to that schedule, notes, and the Schedule of Findings and Questioned Costs. Total federal awards expended were $15,244,795, with the Coronavirus Relief Fund (CFDA 21.019) identified as the district's single major program against a $750,000 Type A/Type B threshold. Opinions on the financial statements and on major-program compliance were both unmodified, no material weaknesses or audit findings were reported, and the district qualified as a low-risk auditee.

**What it is**
Troy School District Federal Awards Supplemental Information (marked "Draft") for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2021, prepared for the Board of Education. Contents run: Report on Schedule of Expenditures of Federal Awards Required by the Uniform Guidance (p. 1); Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting and on Compliance and Other Matters under Government Auditing Standards (p. 2); Report on Compliance for Each Major Federal Program and Report on Internal Control Over Compliance Required by the Uniform Guidance (pp. 3-4); Schedule of Expenditures of Federal Awards (pp. 5-9); Reconciliation of Basic Financial Statements Federal Revenue with the Schedule (p. 10); Notes (p. 11); Schedule of Findings and Questioned Costs (p. 12).

All three reports are dated October 5, 2021. The audit of the basic financial statements produced an unmodified opinion. No deficiencies in internal control over financial reporting were identified that the auditors consider material weaknesses, and tests disclosed no instances of noncompliance required to be reported under Government Auditing Standards. Compliance for the major federal program received an unmodified opinion, and no material weaknesses in internal control over compliance were identified.

**Agenda item**
Item 2.B. under Recognition, dated 10.19.21, on the Troy School District Board of Education agenda: "2022 National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists." The recommendation is to adopt the accompanying resolution, with blank lines for the moving and supporting members and for recording the YES and NO tallies.

**Scale of the program**
More than one million students nationwide, from some 21,000 high schools, entered the National Merit Scholarship Program; only 16,000 of those seniors are selected to be semifinalists. Student achievement is honored through the National Merit Scholarship semifinalist and finalist recognition programs. 2021_24_5_d_11042021_policy_recommendati.paragraph: Business Office memorandum dated Thursday, November 4, 2021 from Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, to Superintendent of Schools Dr. Rich Machesky, copied to Judy Holmes, forwarding policy additions and changes recommended by Administration and the Policy Committee for Board of Education approval. Three items are proposed: a notice-period change to the special meetings provision of Section 1002/1000.02 for compliance with Michigan's Open Meetings Act, 15.261, et seq.; a rewritten Student Bullying subpolicy under Policy 2006/2000.06 to comply with MCL 380.1310b; and a new "Animals on District Property" policy in the 8000 section prompted by increased requests for therapy and service animals.
2021_24_5_d_11042021_policy_recommendati.page:
**Memorandum details**
From the Business Office at 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; phone 248.823.4022, fax 248.823.4013. TO: Dr. Rich Machesky, Superintendent of Schools. FROM: Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services. CC: Judy Holmes. RE: Policy Update Considerations for Board of Education. DATE: Thursday, November 4, 2021. Administration and the Policy Committee recommend the listed policy additions and changes be approved by the Board of Education.

**Section 1002/1000.02 - Special Meetings**
Recommended for compliance with Michigan's Open Meetings Act, 15.261, et seq. The revised provision reads that special meetings of the Board may be called by the President or any three (3) Board members by providing "not less than 2418 hours' notice" to all Board members; the extracted text runs the struck-through existing figure and the underlined replacement figure together at that point. The notice to Board members and the public shall be consistent in manner and form with the requirements of the OMA.

**Student Bullying subpolicy - Policy 2006/2000.06**
Revised to comply with MCL 380.1310b. The Board prohibits bullying "at school" as defined in the policy, as well as off-campus conduct that could likely lead to a material or substantial disruption of the school learning environment. The policy protects all students regardless of the subject matter or motivation for the behavior, prohibits retaliation and false accusations, and keeps the identity of a reporter confidential. Key structural elements:

| Element | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Responsible School Official | The principal of each school building implements the policy for that building |
| Publication | Superintendent revises the Student Code of Conduct and posts the policy on the District website |
| Reporting | Superintendent reports annually to the Board all verified incidents of bullying and consequences imposed |
| Administrative regulations | Procedures for reporting, prompt investigation by the building principal or designee, parent/guardian notification of both claimed victim and alleged perpetrator, confidentiality of reporters, documentation of incidents, and the annual Board report |

Definitions cover "bullying" (written, verbal, physical, or electronic acts, including cyberbullying, that substantially interfere with educational opportunities, place a student in reasonable fear of physical harm or cause substantial emotional distress, have a substantial detrimental effect on physical or mental health, or substantially disrupt school operations), with physical, verbal, and psychological examples; "at school" (classroom, school premises, school bus or other school-related vehicle, and school-sponsored activities on or off premises, including off-premises use of a telecommunications access device or service provider owned or controlled by the District); and "cyberbullying" with four enumerated clauses (i) through (iv). Further sections address Accountability and Retaliation, and state that intentionally false reports may result in disciplinary action.

**New policy - Animals on District Property (8000 section)**
Proposed in response to increased requests for use of therapy and service animals. The draft recognizes that animals are present on District property for many reasons, are commonly utilized by teachers during classroom presentations, and are often housed in classrooms and other campus locations; and that employees, students, parents, vendors, and other members of the public may be accompanied at school by a service or therapy animal in accordance with Federal and State law and the policy. The policy applies to all animals on District property, including service animals, and directs the Superintendent to promulgate consistent administrative regulations.
2021_24_5_d_11042021_policy_recommendati.verbose:
Troy School District Business Office memorandum, agenda item 5.D. for the November 16, 2021 Board of Education meeting, transmitting policy update considerations.

**Header.** Business Office, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; Phone 248.823.4022; Fax 248.823.4013. TO: Dr. Rich Machesky, Superintendent of Schools. FROM: Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services. CC: Judy Holmes. RE: Policy Update Considerations for Board of Education. DATE: Thursday, November 4, 2021. Opening line: "Administration and the Policy Committee recommend the following policy additions/changes be approved by the Board of Education."

**Section 1002/1000.02, Special Meetings.** Recommended "to ensure compliance with Michigan's Open Meetings Act, 15.261, et seq." The provision as presented reads: "Special meetings of the Board may be called by the President or any three (3) Board members by providing not less than 2418 hours' notice to all Board members. The notice to Board members and the public shall be consistent in manner and form with the requirements of the OMA." The memo marks its revisions by underlining; extraction has flattened the strikethrough and underline formatting, leaving the old and new notice-period figures printed adjacent to one another as "2418 hours."

**Student Bullying subpolicy, typically found under Policy 2006/2000.06.** Presented as underlined changes to comply with MCL 380.1310b.

Preamble: The Board recognizes that bullying and cyberbullying significantly interfere with the learning process. Through this Policy, the Board prohibits bullying "at school," as defined below, as well as off-campus conduct that could likely lead to a material or substantial disruption of the school learning environment for one or more students. The Policy is intended to protect all students from bullying, regardless of the subject matter or motivation for the behavior. It also prohibits retaliation or false accusations against a target of bullying, a witness, or another person with reliable information about an act of bullying. The identity of an individual who reports an act of bullying shall remain confidential. The Superintendent will promulgate administrative regulations to implement the policy.

Implementation. Responsible School Official: the principal of each school building is responsible for implementing this Policy for the school to which he or she is assigned. Publication: the Superintendent shall revise the District's Student Code of Conduct, consistent with this Policy, to specifically prohibit bullying and cyberbullying, and is directed to post this Policy on the District's website. Reporting: the Superintendent shall report to the Board of Education, on an annual basis, all verified incidents of bullying, and the resulting consequences that were imposed.

Administrative Regulations. The Superintendent shall promulgate regulations including: a procedure for an individual to report an act of bullying; a procedure for the prompt investigation of a report of an act of bullying by the building principal or his/her designee; a procedure for providing notification to the parent or guardian of both the claimed victim of an act of bullying and the parent or guardian of the alleged perpetrator; a procedure to protect the confidentiality of a person making a report of bullying; a procedure for documenting any prohibited bullying incident that is reported; and the procedure for the Superintendent's annual report to the Board of all verified incidents of bullying and the consequences imposed.

Definitions. "Bullying" means any written, verbal or physical act, or any electronic communication, including but not limited to cyberbullying, that is intended or that a reasonable person would know is likely to harm one or more District students, either directly or indirectly, by substantially interfering with educational opportunities, benefits or programs; adversely affecting a student's ability to participate in or benefit from educational programs or activities by placing a student in reasonable fear of physical harm or by causing substantial emotional distress; having an actual and substantial detrimental effect on a student's physical or mental health; or causing substantial disruption in, or substantial interference with, the orderly operation of the school. Examples listed are Physical (hitting, kicking, spitting, pushing, pulling; taking and/or damaging a person's belongings; extorting money; blocking or impeding student movement; unwelcome physical contact; punching, shoving, poking, choking, pulling hair, beating, biting, throwing objects), Verbal (taunting, malicious teasing, insulting, hurtful name-calling, making threats, gossiping), and Psychological (spreading rumors, manipulating social relationships, coercion, engaging in social exclusion/shunning, extortion or intimidation).

"At school" means in a classroom, anywhere else on school premises, on a school bus or other school-related vehicle, and at a school-sponsored activity or event, whether or not held on school premises; it includes the off-premises use of a telecommunications access device or telecommunications service provider if the device or service provider is owned by or under the control of the District.

"Cyberbullying" means any electronic communication that is intended or that a reasonable person would know is likely to harm one or more pupils either directly or indirectly by: (i) substantially interfering with educational opportunities, benefits or programs; (ii) adversely affecting a student's ability to participate in or benefit from educational programs or activities by placing a student in reasonable fear of physical harm or by causing substantial emotional distress; (iii) having an actual and substantial detrimental effect on a student's physical or mental health; or (iv) causing substantial disruption in, or substantial interference with, the orderly operation of the school.

Accountability. Each student in the School District is accountable for his/her own behavior, based on age-appropriate expectations. The Board believes standards for student behavior must be set cooperatively through interaction among students, parents/guardians, staff, and community members, producing an atmosphere that encourages students to grow in self-discipline. Respect for all students is part of a safe and healthy learning environment, demonstrated through the give-and-take of friendships, group cooperation, social interaction, compromise, and acceptance of differences among other students and staff.

Retaliation. Retaliation against a target of bullying, a witness, another person with reliable information about an act of bullying, or any person who reports, is thought to have reported, files a complaint, or otherwise participates in an investigation or inquiry concerning allegations of bullying is prohibited and will not be tolerated. Such retaliation is a serious violation of Board policy independent of whether a complaint is found to have been substantiated, and suspected reprisal or retaliation should be reported in the same manner as bullying. Making intentionally false reports about bullying for the purpose of getting someone in trouble is similarly prohibited. Retaliation and intentionally false reports may result in disciplinary action. The Superintendent is directed to implement the Policy and is authorized to promulgate such administrative regulations as may be deemed necessary.

**Animals on District Property, proposed for the 8000 section of the policy manual.** Introduced with the observation that requests for use of therapy and service animals have increased. Proposed text: "The Board of Education recognizes that there are many occasions when animals are present on District property and many reasons for those animals' presence. Animals are commonly utilized by teachers during classroom presentations and are often housed in classrooms and other locations on campus. Additionally, employees, students, parents, vendors, and other members of the public may be accompanied at school by a service or therapy animal in accordance with Federal and State law and this policy. This policy applies to all animals on District property, including service animals. The Superintendent will promulgate administrative regulations consistent with this policy."

The memorandum contains no dollar amounts, contract parties, vote records, or millage figures; it is a policy transmittal only.
